scores.notes: One moment at night: the kneeling king presses his ring into a clay lump at the pit's rim while attendants rope a boulder toward the lidded den (right) and torch-bearing lords watch. The clay sits on the paving, and the den has both a lid and a barred side gate. Both are odd, but neither is a contradiction or a second moment.

The temple is drawn twice: a gold temple with two pillars and a bronze basin in a walled court (mid-left), and a second temple facade with paired bronze pillars and carved doors directly behind Hezekiah (right). The pale top-left sky is accepted.

Two near-identical long-haired, bearded Jesus figures in dark grey robes appear, one under the central colonnade and one by the brazier at right. The second is a prominent figure the scene does not ask for.

At heavy zoom, a dashed line ending in a small loop-and-V mark sits on the plaster at the far left edge beside the door (about x=30-50, y=385). At normal and native size it is a barely visible speck, not legible lettering. Isaiah steadying the bowed man in the Jerusalem street at dawn is right.

Two veiled, woman-like faces sit in the second row of the disciples in the boat (left). They are small group members with no role, not prominent figures. Peter leaping with his coat, the pointing disciple, the net and Jesus by the fire are as asked, and the pale top sky is accepted.

The sea is not divided into dry ground: between the two curling wave walls (left and right), open water runs to the horizon, with only a wet strand and debris in the foreground. The central action of the moment is missing. The radiant cloud (top centre) has no figure.

The grey silhouette on the wall behind David (right) falls on the side away from the lamp stand to his left, so it reads as his own cast shadow, not a separate spirit figure. The spirit appears only as the formless dark mass along the ceiling.
The bottom edge is painted tan floor wash across its full width, and the other edges are painted walls, doorway and lamplit wall. There is no bare paper, band or vignette at any edge.

The marks on the paving stone in the bottom-left corner are faint dashes and curls, the same pen texture used across the stones. At native size they are near-invisible, and even zoomed they do not form legible glyphs.

The Queen (right, on the dais) has a black bun, a tiny perched crown and a high white stand-up collar, a clear echo of the animated-film Queen of Hearts. The crown-bearing Knave (centre-left) is a full human body in puffed striped sleeves and breeches wearing a card tabard, not a flat oblong card.

Jesus stands in the bright cave mouth with his arm raised, calling, and Martha kneels at centre in the rock tomb, so the subject, action and place are shown. Lazarus already sitting lit among the mourners (left) is a staging contradiction, not a wrong scene.

In the foreground goat group (lower left), the white goat has no head of its own: its neck runs straight into the brown goat's drinking head, so the two animals are fused. Moses, Aaron, the water and the people are otherwise as asked.

The pale area at the top-right edge is a reserved-white cloud bounded by blue wash and foliage. The top-left corner is a painted cream house wall, and every edge carries wash with no blank band or fade into paper.
The paper in the station-master's hand (lower right) shows only a fine ruled grid of tiny ticks. At normal size there are no legible glyphs or numerals on it or anywhere else.

Only after contrast enhancement does a very faint looped scratch show on the floor in the bottom-right corner. It matches the scattered floor texture nearby and is not visible as writing at normal size. The restrained Levite scene is as asked.

Darius leans over the rim (left) while attendants with a rope lead the calm, unharmed Daniel away from the resting lions, so the rescue from the den is recognisable. That the attendants stand in the pit and pull sideways rather than up is a staging contradiction, not a wrong scene.

One unified scene: Isaiah looks up in a smoke-filled temple hall with gold lamp stands while seraphim hover above. The coal-bearing seraph (upper right) is a later-verse element within the same vision, not a contradiction, and the two-winged form breaks the creature rule rather than changing the subject, action or place.

David follows through with his sling (left) while the armoured Goliath (centre right), struck, reels in a burst of dust with his spear and shield flying, and both armies watch from the slopes. He topples backward rather than onto his face, a detail difference rather than a wrong action.

Alice aims an ordinary pink croquet mallet at the hedgehog, with the flamingo merely carried under her arm. The card soldiers (left) march upright instead of doubling over into arches, and a metal hoop stands at right, so the live-mallet, soldier-arch croquet action is not shown.

A small child sits among the disciples at the boat's rail (left, by the lantern). It is a minor group member, not a prominent figure. Peter stepping onto the stormy water toward Jesus with the boat and lantern behind is as asked.

A tiny dark 'eu'-like dab on the pavement at lower left (about x=300-330, y=745) sits among similar pitting marks and is ambiguous texture rather than legible writing. The wash stops short of the left edge, leaving a pale paper strip down its full height (accepted).

The coal-bearing seraph at top centre has a blank, featureless face. All seraphim have two to four wings with bare, uncovered feet, which breaks the rule that visionary creatures follow the text (six wings covering face and feet). Isaiah, the hovering seraphim, the smoke and the temple hall themselves are shown.

Holmes holds up the single blue stone at the window, but the open strongbox on the desk (left) is heaped with dozens of identical blue gems, with another loose on the desk, contradicting the one unique carbuncle.

Peter, his coat clutched to his chest, strides off the boat's side through the very shallow water's edge toward Jesus by the charcoal fire, while the beloved disciple points from the boat and the others haul the net. A stride rather than a leap, with Jesus nearer than distant, is a detail difference from the shallow-water plunge asked for.

The lit wall right of the doorway at lower right (about x1225-1265, y565-620) carries a stacked column of ink glyphs (=, a hooked 3-like character with small strokes, a 7-like hook) that reads as a wall inscription. The bottom-right corner and the radiance at top centre run to near-white paper (accepted).

The hanging behind Saul's raised arm (upper left, about x60-280, y0-280) has rows of 2-3 px dark flecks that read as woven or coarse texture at normal size; no legible glyph or character shape resolves even at 4x.

The distant card soldier right of centre (about x1120-1165, y340-410) shows only three red diamond suit pips, with no index letters or numerals; pips are the card motif the depiction rules call for, not an inscription.

There is a water wall only on the right; on the left the crowd walks beside a palm-lined beach, dunes and cliffs, with the left wave far behind, and open sea lies ahead at the horizon. The crowd is on a shoreline, not on the sea floor between two walls of water.

The arch soldiers at left and right are oblong cards bent over into arches, with heads and striped arms and legs, which matches soldiers doubled up to make arches; the standing soldiers are flat cards. There is no gore and no screen likeness.
The Hatter's pocket watch (about x795, y465) is a dial about 30 px across with blurred hour-tick blobs and no legible numerals; the hat has no label and nothing else carries writing.

The Caterpillar on the mushroom (right) has an old man's human face and wears a bowler hat and a red waistcoat, though the text gives it no dress, so it is not drawn as an animal as the rule requires.

A third man stands on the road at right (about x1090-1230, y235-465): barefoot, in a ragged tunic with a sash, arms flung wide. He is clearly drawn and is the only other figure, and the cast does not ask for him.

Bill appears twice: one green lizard in a navy tailcoat is in mid-air by Alice's hand (about x700-830, y350-490) and a near-identical one stands in the lower-left foreground (about x0-190, y580-750). The jurors stay animals in clothes, which I do not count as breaking the rule.

Jesus stands ankle-deep in shallows a step from the pebble beach at lower right, with the boat beside the shore and the village close by, so the picture reads as wading ashore, not walking on the open sea. The lantern disciple in the boat looks like Jesus but sits among the disciples, which contradicts nothing.

The small bearded man between the drinking donkeys at centre (about x745-805, y475-585) has his head and folded arms on the grey donkey, but his torso merges into the donkey's back and a single thin stick limb hangs in front of the brown donkey's head.

A second Alice in a blue dress and white pinafore sits on the judges' bench beside the King (about x830-880, y140-195), and the bottom-centre juror (about x410-560, y490-740) has a white rabbit's head and long ears fused to a duck's bill, body and feet. The floor papers show only plain dash lines, and floor and wall wash reach every edge.

The lantern arm's white sleeve passes behind the front disciple's head to the rear disciple, giving two hands each (pointing and reaching for the front man, gripping and holding the lantern for the rear one). Dark storm and sea wash reach all four edges, with only small foam flecks.

The bald, mantled Elisha is on the road below Bethel's gate while youths pour out of the gate at upper right with arms raised and mouths open. He faces the viewer, walking away from the gate rather than up toward it, which is a difference of direction and composition; the subject, action and place are shown.

The king presses signet clay onto a loose round stone on the courtyard paving while rope-men drag it to the right. The den at left (about x90-320, y290-520) has its own wooden lid and barred gate, so the stone covers no mouth and the sealing of the den is not shown.
On the top-right tower wall (about x1330-1376, y0-200) the wash stops and bare cream paper with only ink brick lines meets the right edge; the top-left cornice is also near-white paper (accepted).

The robed lion at left (about x130-310, y300-520) has two forepaws crossed under the robe plus a third paw raised behind the mane, as well as two hind legs. Bare white paper shows at top centre and in the top-left corner behind the radiance (accepted).

The chariots run sideways across the foreground bank right beside Moses, while the robed Israelite crowd fills the channel between the water walls behind them. The pursuers are not driving into the sea after the people.
At bottom left the stone wall's wash breaks off and bare cream paper shows along the left edge and corner (about x0-30, y600-768) (accepted).

The tiny chest in the distant street (about x735, y410) is about 25 px across, and its panel holds 2-3 indistinct dots that show only at 8x, not legible glyphs. The light rays fade to near-white paper at the top-centre edge (about x560-860) (accepted).

The pillar of fire at top centre (about x690-910, y70-320) has a rounded, head-like crown above horizontal outstretched arm-bars and a column that flares at the base like a robe. At full size it reads as a cruciform human-shaped figure of fire standing for God, though it has no face.
All four corners and edge strips carry wash (grey-cream ceiling, ochre walls, dark floor), with no blank band, white vignette or bare paper at any edge.

A second straight stick (about x240-320, y330-680) leans with its top against the underside of David's elbow while he grips the crook. It is an odd extra prop but physically possible, and no pose, object or place is contradictory.

The man-faced creature (about x860-1000, y180-450) has a photographic, out-of-style head on a winged robe, with wings in place of arms. The face itself is not malformed and there is no extra or broken limb; the lion, ox and eagle limbs read correctly.
